# The Betrayal

> The Betrayal (thebetrayal.co.uk) is a party game for 8 to 24 players in one room, best with 8 to 16, played on everyone's own phone in the browser. A few players are secretly the Forsworn; the rest, the Loyal, have one evening to find them. It costs £10 for one party or £20 a month. It is an independent game made in England and is not affiliated with any television programme or broadcaster.

## Key facts

- What it is: a hidden-role (social deduction) party game for adults, "the party game of loyalty and lies". Always written "The Betrayal", with "The".
- Players: 8 to 24 in one room, best with 8 to 16. Nobody sits out, and the host never sees anyone else's role.
- Length: about an hour for 8 to 10 players; about an hour and a half for 12 to 16; about two hours for 20 to 24. Classic takes longer: about 3 to 3½ hours for 8 to 12 players.
- What you need: a phone each (any browser; no app to download, no account) and a prize. A TV is optional: a laptop connected or casting to it shows the questions, votes and reveals, with music.
- Joining: guests scan the QR code on the TV, or go to thebetrayal.co.uk/join and type the six-character Table code and their name.
- Prize: set by the host. By default, chocolate coins: one coin for every 100 points the winners take from the Purse.
- Price: a Table is £10 for one party of 8 to 24, open for 48 hours from the first use of its booking code. A Regular is £20 a month: one booking code that opens a new Table whenever you like, one at a time; cancel any time. Payments by Stripe. Prices include VAT where it applies.
- How to buy: https://thebetrayal.co.uk/buy. The booking code (OATH-XXXX-XXXX) is shown on screen straight after payment; enter it on the home page to open a Table.
- Contact: info@thebetrayal.co.uk or https://thebetrayal.co.uk/contact

## How a game works (Modern, everyone on their own phone)

1. The host opens the Table with their booking code and name; guests join on their phones.
2. The Oath: each phone privately asks its player whether they would like to be Forsworn, then deals the roles. The Forsworn (about one player in four or five: 2 for 8 to 10 players, 3 for 11 to 15, 4 for 16 to 22, 5 for 23 or 24) see each other; nobody else sees anything.
3. Trials: party games played on the phones (quizzes, word games, guessing games, charades where only the actor sees the word, rock-paper-scissors and more; 15 in all, drawing on thousands of questions and prompts). They fill a shared Purse and win Sanctuary, protection from that night.
4. The Reckoning: a few minutes of debate on a timer, then a secret vote on every phone. The player with the most votes is exiled and their role is revealed.
5. Night: the Forsworn choose someone to poison. Everyone else taps a name too, so nobody can tell who is choosing. At dawn the victim, told first in secret on their phone, announces it and gets thirty seconds of last words.
6. Players who are out become Ghosts: they stay at the party and still call each vote.
7. The final starts with five or fewer players. The survivors decide in secret whether they trust everyone left; then the Unmasking reveals every role. The Loyal win if every Forsworn is gone and take the Purse they built; the Forsworn win if one survives and take what the Purse fell short of its target. The game ends with up to six awards.

Classic is the other way to play every Table, for a longer, more immersive evening of about three hours: a TV with a laptop, one phone for a Keeper who reads the script and doesn't play, blindfolds at night and votes chalked on small boards. Classic also has a Short game of about 2 to 2½ hours for 8 to 10 players.

## Comparisons

- The Betrayal is similar in idea to the TV show The Traitors (hidden traitors, a vote each day, a victim each night), but it is an original game that you play yourselves at home, and it is not connected to The Traitors, the BBC or its makers.
- It is often used as an alternative to a murder mystery party: no scripts, characters or booklets, nobody knows the answer in advance, and it works for any number from 8 to 24.
- Occasions: games nights, birthday parties, Christmas and office parties, hen and stag dos, dinner parties (in Classic, dinner in courses is served between the rounds).
